comparator.name: Physics
comparator.sourceNotes: The official 2026-2027 Teaching and Examination Regulations define a mandatory 150-EC Physics major and a 30-EC free minor. The pathway below accounts for the complete 180 EC. Wherever the major requires a restricted choice, the first-listed option is used as the neutral official-order tie-break: Introduction to Astronomy in Year 1, Biomaterials 1 in Year 2, and Nanophysics and Nanotechnology plus Advanced Electrodynamics in Year 3. The genuine 30-EC minor remains open rather than being populated with an invented specialization. No formal route is defined.

exception.reason: The University of Groningen programme is a full disciplinary Physics degree. Its 150-EC major integrates calculus, linear algebra, differential equations and computational methods with classical and relativistic mechanics, electromagnetism, quantum physics, thermal and statistical physics, waves and optics, atomic and solid-state physics, electronics, subatomic physics, nanophysics, advanced electrodynamics, multiple staged physics laboratories and a 15-EC physics research project. UCR offers a useful mathematics and computation sequence and some applications in energy, earth systems, imaging and robotics, but it offers no Physics or Astronomy courses and no experimental-physics laboratory sequence. A UCR programme assembled from mathematics, computing and sustainability courses would be a coherent quantitative or energy-systems pathway, not a defensible Physics comparator.
exception.curriculumContext: The official 2026-2027 regulations account for the full 180 EC as a mandatory 150-EC Physics major plus a 30-EC free minor. Year one comprises 60 EC in calculus, computational methods, differential equations, electricity and magnetism, linear algebra, mechanics and relativity, physics laboratory skills and research, and one 5-EC introductory physics or astronomy choice. Year two comprises 60 EC in advanced physics laboratory work, computational methods, electronics, subatomic physics, two sequential quantum-physics courses, atoms and solids, thermal physics, waves and optics, and one 5-EC choice. The remaining major comprises ethics and professional aspects, two advanced choices and a 15-EC bachelor research project; the 30-EC minor completes Year three. The live programme page likewise describes a broad, mathematically grounded, experimental Physics bachelor totaling 180 EC.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR workbook rows, including course descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned Fall 2026 cohort terms. DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods, DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH213 Computational & Numerical Methods, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus, DISMATH312 Linear Systems and DISMATH314 Probability & Statistics provide relevant mathematical foundations in calculus, differential equations, matrices, numerical algorithms, transforms, signals, systems and statistics. DISGATE101 Introduction to Programming supplies Python and computational problem-solving; DISDATA212 Image Processing & Computer Vision and DISDATA312 Robotics apply mathematical and computational methods to imaging, kinematics and motion. ENSENVI111 Dynamic Earth includes a broad introduction to geophysics, ENSENVI213 Earth System Science Tools uses quantitative modelling, and ENSSUST111 Climate Change and ENSSUST311 Renewable System Design address climate and energy applications. The workbook nevertheless contains no course in classical or relativistic mechanics, electromagnetism, quantum physics, thermodynamics or statistical physics, waves or physical optics, atomic or solid-state physics, electronics, subatomic or particle physics, astronomy, nanophysics or advanced electrodynamics. It also contains no experimental-physics laboratory progression: HCBLIFE214 Life Science Laboratory is explicitly biochemical and molecular, not physical. ENSSUST211 Energy & Sustainability has no planned availability for the Fall 2026 cohort and in any event is a multidisciplinary sustainability course rather than disciplinary physics. No available sequence culminates in an equivalent 15-EC experimental Physics research project. The mathematical and applied-science strengths therefore cover only supporting tools and selected applications, not the defining Physics curriculum.
